method: Human visual inspection of every WebP against its manifest scene, target sentence, and displayed objects/actions.

findings.before: The image showed repeated phone notifications but did not identify the male person referred to by ‘He’.
findings.fix: Replaced the illustration with one that shows repeated calls from the same identifiable male contact and the learner's frustration.
findings.after: The subject, pronoun, repeated action, and emotional meaning now match ‘He’s getting on my nerves.’

findings.questionIds: The 30 legacy expansion questions ending in extra-visual-1 through extra-visual-5
findings.before: The first six lessons had no visual questions, so learners could not practise matching these lesson phrases to concrete scenes.
findings.fix: Created and inspected five lesson-specific WebP illustrations for each of the six lessons, then checked every image against its manifest scene, target sentence, distractors, alt text, hint, and explanations.
findings.after: All six lessons now have five visually distinct questions whose target meaning is supported by the visible action and whose distractors describe materially different situations.

findings.before: The first generated versions used ambiguous analog clocks that did not reliably distinguish the first half from the second half.
findings.fix: Rejected both drafts and regenerated them with clear digital match clocks showing 32:00 and 78:00.
findings.after: The goal scene is unambiguously before halftime and the excited late-match scene is unambiguously in the second half.
